key_insight: Strain controls how neighboring iodine vacancies reconfigure in CsPbI3, with compression favoring separation and tension favoring pair-preserving relay hopping under isotropic deformation.
engineering_relevance: Strain and vacancy-pair orientation may offer design levers for managing defect migration and structural stability in halide perovskites.
method: Machine-learning molecular dynamics of neighboring iodine vacancies in tilted CsPbI3.
Isotropic and biaxial strain to probe hopping and pair reconfiguration.
Static DFT and SevenNet-0 calculations of vacancy interactions.
evidence_signal: Trajectories show nonmonotonic short-time hopping fractions and orientation-dependent responses to biaxial compression, while static calculations find repulsive interactions in every configuration examined.
watch_item: Short-time hopping behavior does not establish long-term vacancy-pair stability or device-scale degradation rates.
paper_title: Strain-dependent Dynamics of Interactions of Iodine-vacancy pairs in CsPbI3: A DFT and Machine-Learning Molecular Dynamics Study
